title: 2016 AMC 10A Problem 21
statement: Circles with centers \(P,\) \(Q\) and \(R,\) having radii \(1,\) \(2\) and \(3,\) respectively, lie on the same side of line \(l\) and are tangent to \(l\) at \(P',\) \(Q'\) and \(R',\) respectively, with \(Q'\) between \(P'\) and \(R'.\) The circle with center \(Q\) is externally tangent to each of the other two circles. What is the area of \(\triangle PQR?\)

solutions.text:
Put the tangent line on the \(x\)-axis and take \(P=(0,1).\) Because \(PQ=1+2=3\) and the centers differ in height by \(1,\) the horizontal distance from \(P\) to \(Q\) is \[\sqrt{3^2-1^2}=2\sqrt2.\] Similarly, \(QR=2+3=5\) and its centers also differ in height by \(1,\) so their horizontal distance is \(2\sqrt6.\)

Thus we may use \[ \begin{aligned} P&=(0,1),\qquad Q=(2\sqrt2,2), \\ R&=(2\sqrt2+2\sqrt6,3). \end{aligned} \] The coordinate-area formula gives \[ \begin{aligned} [PQR] &=\frac12\left|4\sqrt2-(2\sqrt2+2\sqrt6)\right| \\ &=\sqrt6-\sqrt2. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: Use horizontal distances between tangent points
Use those horizontal distances in a coordinate-area formula
